title: Finite type algebras with finite fibre at a minimal prime become finite after one localization
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $S$ is generated by finitely many elements as an $R$-algebra. Let $\mathfrak p$ be a minimal prime ideal of $R$ (a prime containing no strictly smaller prime). Suppose the set of prime ideals $\mathfrak q$ of $S$ with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$ is finite. Then there is $g\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that $S_{\varphi(g)}$ is a finitely generated module over $R_g$ via the induced homomorphism $R_g\to S_{\varphi(g)}$, where the rings are localizations obtained by inverting the indicated elements [def-weil-ring-localization-away].
